title: The Perfect Confession Again
premise: When Coral Marchetti is summoned to probate a second will for town founder Edmund Hale—one dated after his death and naming a beneficiary no one can find—the empty coffin discovered during a routine exhumation shatters the town's carefully maintained fiction that Hale died peacefully fifteen years ago. Coral, who has spent his career as the keeper of Ashford Hollow's secrets, realizes the missing beneficiary, Vera Okafor, is the same woman the town officially declared dead a decade ago and whom he himself once helped disappear. As the district attorney weaponizes the empty coffin to reopen a murder case against Coral's oldest client, Coral must choose between the alphabetized safety of his double life and the living, breathing witness everyone swears is dead. In the end, Coral produces Vera at trial, confesses his own role in the original cover-up, and accepts disbarment—discovering that belonging to a town means belonging to its guilt, not just its filing cabinets.
about_author: Beatrix Thornbury is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade watching wills, deeds, and secrets pass across her desk. She writes mysteries about the quiet professionals who keep towns running—and the paperwork that eventually betrays them.

chapters.title: The Second Will
chapters.summary: Coral Marchetti's POV. Coral is handed a second will for Edmund Hale, dated three days after the death certificate, leaving everything to a Vera Okafor. His practiced calm masks a spike of recognition—he knows that name. Emotional beat: the first crack in fifteen years of controlled invisibility.

chapters.title: Exhumation Order
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The contested will forces an exhumation; Coral attends the graveside hoping to manage the spectacle. The coffin is opened and found empty. The town's grief curdles into suspicion, and DA Renata Voss locks eyes with Coral across the hole. Emotional beat: dread—the ground itself has broken its promise.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with a flashback to fifteen years earlier. We learn Coral helped a frightened woman named Vera Okafor vanish after witnessing something in Hale's house, filing her out of existence as thoroughly as any deed. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing through the tidy architecture of his memory.

chapters.title: The Widow's Ledger
chapters.summary: Margaret Hale's POV. Edmund's widow, who signed the death certificate, privately confesses to Coral that her husband isn't dead—he's been living under an assumed name and paying her hush money. She hands Coral a ledger of payments. Emotional beat: complicity wearing the mask of mourning.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. DA Voss charges Coral's oldest client, town doctor Priya Nand, with falsifying the death certificate, and subpoenas Coral's files. Coral must decide which documents to surrender, knowing one folder holds Vera's trail. Emotional beat: the law he served turning into a trap of his own making.

chapters.title: A Woman Made of Paper
chapters.summary: Vera Okafor's POV, revealed mid-book. Vera has built a life two states away, but the will—her name in print—has flushed her out. She returns to Ashford Hollow in disguise, watching Coral's office from across the square. Emotional beat: terror and longing; a ghost deciding to be seen.

chapters.title: The Night at Hale House
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Coral and Vera, converging in flashbacks and the present. The truth of fifteen years ago emerges: Vera witnessed Hale kill his business partner, and the town's leading families buried the crime along with the empty coffin. Emotional beat: two witnesses to the same night finally speaking it aloud.

chapters.title: Burn the Files
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Voss offers Coral immunity to testify against Priya; someone ransacks his office and steals the ledger. Coral realizes the founding families, led by Margaret's son, will kill to keep the coffin empty in every sense. Emotional beat: the keeper of secrets becomes their target.

chapters.title: The Perfect Confession
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, climax. At trial, Coral takes the stand uninvited, confesses his role in erasing Vera, and produces her in the courtroom—alive, sworn, and naming Edmund Hale as a murderer. The gallery erupts; Voss must choose between her case and the truth. Emotional beat: liberation through self-destruction.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, resolution. Disbarred but unburied, Coral watches Hale get indicted and the town begin its slow, painful reckoning. Priya is freed; Vera stays, opening a bookshop on the square. Coral is asked to stay too—not as the town's filing cabinet, but as one of its flawed citizens. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
